edges.notes: KVM is a Linux kernel virtualization subsystem exposing hardware-assisted virtualization to userspace per kernel documentation.
Firecracker requires KVM on supported Linux hosts per upstream Firecracker documentation.
Contrasting isolation models: KVM runs guests with separate kernel contexts vs namespaces isolating processes within one kernel.
cgroups limit host resources for processes; KVM guests are a different abstraction layer from cgroup-scoped containers.
Docker Engine’s default Linux containers use namespaces/cgroups; KVM addresses hardware virtualization, not the same mechanism.
Kubernetes can orchestrate KVM-backed runtimes in some stacks (e.g. VM-class sandboxes); distinct from default OCI Linux containers.
Confidential VMs may compose KVM-style virtualization with TEE hardware features depending on platform and stack.
KVM guests commonly attach virtio paravirtual devices; virtio is the device transport, KVM is the hypervisor API.
KVM-hosted virtio guests may use vhost backends on the host for efficient I/O; KVM is VM control, vhost is the I/O path.
KVM guests may attach devices via VFIO-mediated passthrough; KVM is the hypervisor API, VFIO is the device/IOMMU assignment path.
QEMU drives KVM on Linux hosts for hardware-accelerated virtualization; KVM is the kernel API, QEMU is the userspace VMM.
libvirt commonly orchestrates KVM-backed QEMU domains on Linux; KVM is the hypervisor API, libvirt is the management layer.
KubeVirt VM workloads use KVM-backed QEMU on Linux nodes; KVM is the kernel API, KubeVirt orchestrates via Kubernetes.
Kata Containers accelerates guest VMs with KVM on Linux nodes; KVM is the kernel API, Kata composes it for OCI execution.
